newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures erode again late, end off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures erode again late, end off.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures eroded again in late trading, finishing a choppy session mostly weaker but little changed on the day.
"It was pretty thin and sloppy," said a floor analyst of afternoon trading conditions, in which locals dominated with dealers showing occasional interest.

Late erosion in U.S. Treasury bond futures, coupled with some long profit-aking heading into next week's full lineup of U.S. economic reports, pushed September Standard & Poor's 500 futures back down after a midday partial recovery from a late-morning pullback.

Even though S&P 500 futures still appeared technically overbought and could prove vulnerable to a bout of long profit-taking, the floor analyst said that given the market's recent history, any sharp pullbacks might be greeted as buying opportunities.
A floor broker said that any rally back above the new all-time peak at 951.75, which the contract set early Friday morning as T-bond futures firmed, could usher in a further rally toward 955.40.
Futures also seesawed in tandem with high-technology stocks, which alternately rose and fell Friday.
Futures had sprinted upward from a strong opening to their highest price ever as T-bond futures moved slightly higher on a weaker than forecast June U.S. existing home sales report.
The market had only a momentary downtick on a stronger than expected level of June U.S. durable goods orders.
Fair value Friday for nearby S&Ps was about 5.35 points premium. Arbitrage buy programs needed a 6.15-point premium, and sell programs required about 4.55 points over cash.

Sept S&P 500s eased 0.95 pt to 944.90, Nikkei rose 115.0 pts to 20,465.0, Midcap 400s lost 0.40 to 309.10, Russell fell 0.30 to 410.25, and NASDAQ fell 3.75 to 1092.50. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
